item.description:
Closing a file takes you back

Wortel 2026.41.6 · 2026-10-07

Closing a file takes you back. Double-click a file in Changes or History, read it, close it, and you’re back where you opened it, not on whichever tab happened to sit next to it. If you switched to another tab in the meantime, the neighbouring tab comes forward, as before.

Menus that say what they’ll do. Check for Updates Automatically and Share Anonymous Usage Data in the Wortel menu now show a checkmark when they’re on. Show and Hide commands for the sidebar, the panes and the side column now name what they’ll actually do, Pin Session reads Unpin Session for a pinned one, and commands that don’t apply right now are greyed out.

Every agent back in its own conversation

Wortel 2026.41.5 · 2026-10-07

Every agent comes back where it was. If Wortel’s sessions end while it’s closed, for example after choosing Stop Running in Background on its Dock icon, reopening Wortel resumes each agent into the conversation it was in. Claude, Pi and Codex come back in their exact conversation, even with two sessions of the same agent in one folder. Other agents continue their latest conversation, as before.

No freeze on reopening. Wortel could hang on launch when a session had been busy while it was closed, for example an agent that kept working. It now reconnects right away, however much happened in the meantime.

A shell that lost its agent gets it back. When an agent ended while Wortel was closed but its terminal stayed open, the session used to come back as a bare prompt. Wortel now starts the agent again in its own conversation.

Updates that land. Updates download quietly in the background. When one is ready, a download icon appears in the sidebar’s bottom bar, and Restart Now takes a second or two, with every session back. Automatic checks are on; you can turn them off in the Wortel menu.

Shortcuts that match other Mac apps. ⇧⌘[ and ⇧⌘] switch tabs, as in Safari and Xcode. ⌥⌘↑ and ⌥⌘↓ move between sessions. ⌃⌘1, ⌃⌘2 and ⌃⌘3 open Changes, History and Files.

Also in this release: Wortel keeps a short log of how each agent exited, so a session that ends unexpectedly can be explained.

A clearer "working", and sections that fold

Wortel 2026.41.4 · 2026-10-06

Working, at a glance. A session with something running used to show a small grey dot breathing slowly, which in dark mode came out nearly black on a dark sidebar. It’s now three small dots in a soft wave, the way a chat app shows someone typing: clearly busy, without asking for anything. The coloured dots still mean something needs you.

Pinned and Sessions fold. Click the Pinned or Sessions header to fold it away, as you can a folder, and Wortel remembers it. A folded section shows a dot when a session inside needs you, and unfolds by itself when a new session lands in it.

Headers you can point at. Folder, Pinned and Sessions headers light up under the pointer like session rows do, so it’s clear they’re there to click.

Also in this release: every status dot in the sidebar now follows light and dark mode when you switch between them.
